name: yum configuration file
description:
We will install couple of yum plugins/utils which we need later.
yum install -y yum-utils createrepo
. Okay now read about config file.
The configuration file for yum and related utilities is located at /etc/yum.conf This file contains
  • one mandatory [main] section, which allows you to set yum options that have global effect.
  • one or more [repository] sections, which allow you to set repository-specific options.
However, it is recommended to define individual repositories in new or existing . repo files in the /etc/yum.repos.d/ directory. You already have sample here installed on this machine. Lets view its content:
cat /etc/yum.conf
The following are the most commonly-used options in the [mai n] section:
cachedir= directory
Use this option to set the directory where yum should store its cache and database files.By default, yum's cache directory is /var/cache/yum/$basearch/$releasever.
exactarch= True/False
With this option, you can set yum to consider exact architecture when updating already installed packages.
assumeyes= 0/1
The assumeyes option determines whether or not yum prompts for confirmation of critical actions.
gpg check= value
Use the gpg check option to specify if yum should perform a GPG signature check on packages.
For a complete list of available [main] options, see the [main] OPTIONS section of the man yum.conf.

name: Setting [repository] Options
description:
The [repository] sections, where repository is a unique repository ID such as my_personal_repo (spaces are not permitted), allow you to define individual yum repositories. The following is a bare-minimum example of the form a [repository] section takes:
[repository]
name=repository_name
baseurl=repository_url
Here, repository_name is a human-readable string describing the repository.
Replace repository_url with a URL to the directory where the repodata directory of a repository is located:
If the repository is available over HTTP, use: http://path/to/repo
If the repository is available over FTP, use: ftp://path/to/repo
    If the repository is local to the machine, use: file:///path/to/local/repo
Other useful [repository] directive are:
enabled = value
This is a simple way to tell yum to use or ignore a particular repository
We will see how to create mariadb repo. Put below content into a file /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb.repo
[mariadb]    
name = MariaDB             
baseurl = http://yum.mariadb.org/10.0/$basearch
Now perform to view the package details.
yum search MariaDB

name: yum variables
description:
You can use and reference the following built-in variables in yum commands and in all yum configuration files
$releasever
You can use this variable to reference the release version of Red Hat Enterprise Linux. Yum obtains the value of $rel easever from the d i stro verpkg = value line in the /etc/yum.conf configuration file. If there is no such line in /etc/yum. conf, then yum infers the correct value by deriving the version number from the redhat-release package.
$arch
You can use this variable to refer to the system's CPU architecture

name: Handle repo using yum-config-manager
description:
To viewing the Current Configuration,type:
yum-config-manager

Adding a Yum repository

To define a new repository, you can either add a [repository] section to the /etc/yum.conf file, or to a .repo file in the /etc/yum.repos.d/ directory. All files with the .repo file extension in this directory are read by yum, and it is recommended to define your repositories here instead of in /etc/yum.conf.
yum-config-manager --add-repo repository_url
where repository_url is a link to the .repo file.

Disabling a Yum Repository

To disable a mariadb yum repository, run the following command as :
yum-config-manager --disable mariadb
(where repository is the unique repository ID use yum repo list all to list available repository ID). Now perform to view the package details.
yum search MariaDB
Cant find it, because disabled mariadb repo.

Enabling a Yum Repository

To enable a particular repository or repositories, type the following at a shell prompt as root:
yum-config-manager --enable mariadb

again do:
yum search MariaDB

name: Creating custom repo
description:
To set up a yum repository, follow these steps:
1. Install the createrepo package. To do so, type the following at a shell prompt as root(we already installed this):
yum install createrepo
2. Copy all packages that you want to have in your repository into one directory, such as /opt/
we will use yum to download rpm, put into under /opt and don't install them with following command
yum install --downloadonly --downloaddir=/opt xfsprogs
check /opt directory for this package.
3. the following command:
createrepo --database /opt
creates the necessary metadata for your yum repository, as well as the sqlite database for speeding up yum operations.
3.3. move all existing repo files to /tmp.
mv /etc/yum.repos.d/*.repo /tmp
so that we know our custom repo is used on for this task.
4. Setup /etc/yum.repos.d/local.repo file with following content:
[local]  
name = localrepo  
baseurl=file:///opt
5.Now perform
'yum search xfsprogs'
You can see our package being fetched from local directory ..right? and go ahead install it,if you want that package.

If you want to set this /opt accessible to other machine on your local network, then you need install web-server say apache and move /opt content into html finally update baseurl as http://hostname/repo on local.repo file.

I hope you have learned about how to setup yum using other repo and create your own repo. See you in next topic!
